target_customer: Ship operators, crew managers and vessel managers at shipping companies
problem: Crew changes, port risk and port agent communication were handled by email and spreadsheets, and COVID-19 rules made crew changes hard to plan.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for maritime operations software, sold per fleet
product_category: Maritime operations software and data platform

founders.name: Nick Clarke
previous_startups: Citadel, maritime security firm founded 2011, ran over 10 years
founders.background_notes: Lloyd's Register article, April 2021. Met Olickel at Entrepreneur First in January 2019.

founders.name: Hrishi Olickel
founders.background_notes: Lloyd's Register article: about 10 years in tech across consumer and deep-tech firms in Southeast Asia, three papers in computer security and HCI, a co-authored fire detection patent. TechCrunch 2021 says his background was in parametric insurance and robotics. Education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating port risk, flight and visa data for over 100,000 ports and building planning tools. Data sourcing and integrations were the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Curated port and crew data and integrations with BIMCO, ATPI and Dataloy help, but data could be rebuilt by well funded maritime software vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found in sources opened.

market_need_then: Lloyd's Register April 2021 reports 25,000 seafarers helped home and over 1,000 vessels served. COVID-19 border rules created acute crew change pain.

branding.domain_note: Uses grey-wing.com, a hyphenated domain for the one-word brand Greywing.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical, emoji in section headers on the current site

branding.brand_signature: Product names Flotilla, CRY4, Landfall, Semaphore and the later Proteus assistant
branding.community_and_virality: Trade press only (Lloyd's Register, Seatrade, TechCrunch). Won the Captain's Table 2020 innovation pitch in November 2020.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive product naming and trade press, but no sourced evidence the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.from: Maritime security marketplace connecting clients with piracy protection solutions
pivots.to: Crew change and port risk tools, then a broader maritime operating system
pivots.why: COVID-19 crew change problems at the start of the pandemic

outcome_analysis: Greywing is active. It started as a maritime security marketplace in May 2019 and pivoted at the start of the pandemic to crew change tools, which won customers like Hafnia and OSM. It raised a 2.5M dollar seed in October 2021 and later added AI assistants (SeaGPT, Proteus). No later round was found. The pivot found real demand and the company stays small, with unclear scale.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch and e27 (no date on e27). ZoomInfo names Signal Ventures as lead, single source, not used. CB Insights lists 2.63M total. Competitor search: the sources opened (TechCrunch, e27, Lloyd's Register) name no competitors and the search surfaced no dated rivals, so the list is empty. YC page lists founding 2019, the site says 2020; Lloyd's Register says May 2019. YC page founders section is empty and Clarke and Olickel come from TechCrunch and Lloyd's Register. Education of founders not found. An outcome search for layoffs or acquisition found nothing.
